claims.text: A machine-learning potential trained on ab initio data can approximate the ab initio potential-energy surface efficiently.
Such a potential can provide accurate free-energy calculations for high-entropy alloys and their binary subsystems.
Such a potential can provide accurate entropy calculations for high-entropy alloys and their binary subsystems.
The proposed workflow will reduce computational cost by one to two orders of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will achieve greater than 90% accuracy for fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
CrMnFeCoNi is an example of the high-entropy-alloy systems targeted by the proposal.
The proposed machine-learning potential will incorporate vibrational contributions.
The proposed machine-learning potential will incorporate anharmonic contributions.
The proposed machine-learning potential will incorporate electron–vibration effects.
Machine-learning potentials can implicitly capture complex structural correlations without an explicitly defined structural mediator.
Approximating the ab initio potential-energy surface enables efficient molecular-dynamics simulations.
These efficient simulations retain the physics necessary for accurate free-energy and entropy calculations.
The proposed method could outperform TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The proposed scope is 300 K to 3000 K.
The proposed compositional scope extends from binary through quinary alloys at varying concentrations.
Training an accurate machine-learning potential for complex high-entropy alloys may be difficult.
